title: B2-Sampling: Fusing Balanced and Biased Sampling for Graph Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Graph contrastive learning must select positive and negative node pairs to learn embedding distances.

gap.claim: Existing approaches face an enormous number of candidate negative pairs and unreliable heuristics that introduce noise into positive and negative pair labels.

contributions.claim: B2-Sampling combines balanced sampling of representative negative pairs using topological and embedding diversity with biased sampling of error-prone negative pairs for label learning and correction.
The balanced and biased sampling procedures can be applied iteratively to discriminate and correct training pairs and support multiple known graph contrastive learning models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe B2-Sampling as a novel sampling approach for addressing the two identified graph contrastive learning challenges in a unified way.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on node classification, node clustering, and graph classification tasks.
The authors report that B2-Sampling significantly improves graph contrastive learning model performance with acceptable runtime overhead.
The authors report that code and additional experiment results are available on the project website.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph contrastive learning is used to learn embeddings in which semantically similar nodes are closer, with positive and negative pairs serving as learning labels.
Existing pair-selection approaches face too many candidate negative pairs and noisy pair labels caused by unreliable heuristics.
B2-Sampling addresses both challenges through balanced sampling of representative negatives and biased sampling to learn and correct error-prone negative-pair labels.
The two sampling procedures can be applied iteratively and support multiple known graph contrastive learning models.
Experiments across node classification, node clustering, and graph classification are reported to show improved performance with acceptable runtime overhead.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates representative negative-pair selection from correction of the most error-prone negative-pair labels.

interpretation.claim: Sampling quality and label reliability can be treated as related but distinct sources of contrastive-learning error.

application.claim: For contrastive objectives with many candidate negatives and noisy pair heuristics, consider combining diversity-aware selection with targeted label correction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson applies beyond graph contrastive learning or under what data conditions it may fail.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, numerical performance gains, or runtime measurements.
The abstract does not describe the sampling algorithms, correction procedure, or implementation details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or the conditions underlying the reported improvements.
